body:
Should this be:
```suggestion
				set_message(TTR("Translating: (0, 0, 0)"));
```
To make it properly localizable? Or is this used elsewhere too? Same below

`TTR("Translating:")` is already used:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2487a297b236e28e8ddf96fa8d6b44a164c7cb2c/editor/scene/3d/node_3d_editor_plugin.cpp#L5896-L5898
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2487a297b236e28e8ddf96fa8d6b44a164c7cb2c/editor/scene/3d/node_3d_editor_plugin.cpp#L3574-L3575

But there's also:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2487a297b236e28e8ddf96fa8d6b44a164c7cb2c/editor/scene/3d/node_3d_editor_plugin.cpp#L6085

Probably all of them should use the same localizable string.

Do we want the vector format to be customizable though? I think it makes sense for the vector formatting to be always the same and thus the localizable string to have only 1 arg/placeholder:

```suggestion
						set_message(vformat(TTR("Translating: %s"), vformat("(%s, %s, %s)",
								String::num(selected_node->get_global_position().x, snap_step_decimals),
								String::num(selected_node->get_global_position().y, snap_step_decimals),
								String::num(selected_node->get_global_position().z, snap_step_decimals)));
```

(alternatively just `TTR("Translating:")` and concatenate the value manually, like it was done in here before the change)

On the other hand `"Translating: (%s, %s, %s)"` probably gives better context for the translators right away. So I'm not sure which one is preferred. @KoBeWi Any thoughts?
Out of curiosity, why not use the `%v` placeholder for Vector3 formatting?

> Out of curiosity, why not use the `%v` placeholder for Vector3 formatting?

Good question. AFAICT it should be fine to be used here, I just didn't think about it (I'd guess this code predates support for `%v` placeholder in the first place?).

```suggestion
						set_message(vformat(TTR("Translating: %s"), vformat("%.*v", snap_step_decimals, selected_node->get_global_position())));
```

Part of the argument for suggesting the change above is that there's been some issues about forcing spacing into translated strings that isn't necessarily suitable for all languages, so allowing the translation to adjust spacing would help with that, as not all languages use spacing in the same places

> Part of the argument for suggesting the change above is that there's been some issues about forcing spacing into translated strings that isn't necessarily suitable for all languages, so allowing the translation to adjust spacing would help with that, as not all languages use spacing in the same places

It's unclear to me which change/suggestion do you refer to. Given:

1. `TTR("Translating:")` + space + value_string
2. `TTR("Translating: %s")`
3. `TTR("Translating: (%s, %s, %s)")`

Are you saying that `2`/`3` are better than `1` as the space preceding the value is contained within the localizatable string?

Are you saying that `3` is better than `2`?
Only that 2/3 is better than 1, not sure how the localization aspect applies to numbers and formatting for that

I'll be honest, I'm not sure what the ask is since I'm not familiar with all the intricacies of localization besides just generally being aware that some languages read right to left or have no spaces between words. 

We should probably make some kind of comprehensive guideline, but I'm not sure what that is just from reading the conversation above.

@ryevdokimov I think `TTR("Translating: %s")` is the way to go, and as suggested by Calinou we could simplify the code by using `%v` placeholder. So here you could apply [my last suggestion](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115855#discussion_r2774143491). I'll add suggestions for other changes. Then I think should be good to merge.
